newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater figure Susan McDougal must stay in jail.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater figure Susan McDougal must stay in jail.

text.p: - Susan McDougal, a former business partner of President Clinton and his wife jailed for refusing to answer questions about their finances lost a bid to be released Thursday.

A federal judge refused to vacate a contempt-of-court citation against McDougal, who remains behind bars in Arkansas because she would not answer questions posed by Whitewater special prosecutors before a federal grand jury.
"Obviously we're disappointed that the judge declined our petition without a hearing," McDougal's attorney, Bobby McDaniel, said.
"We thought our case had some real substance," McDaniel said.
Also Thursday Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth W. Starr agreed to postpone the trial of Clinton's successor as governor of Arkansas.
Jim Guy Tucker, who was convicted of fraud and conspiracy in May in the first jury trial of the Whitewater investigation, was to be tried in December with two other men on a second fraud indictment.

His lawyers had argued that Tucker, who is awaiting a liver transplant because of a degenerative intestinal disorder, could not withstand the stress of a trial and must be prepared to leave Arkansas at a moment's notice for the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota.

Tucker and his co-defendants are accused by Starr of fraud and tax evasion in the sale of a cable television system in which they were involved in the 1980s. All three men have said they are innocent.
McDougal was jailed Sept. 9 after refusing to cooperate with the investigation of the Clintons being conducted by Kenneth W. Starr, the Whitewater special prosecutor.

McDougal and her former husband, James McDougal, were partners with the Clintons in Whitewater, a failed Arkansas real estate project, in the 1970s. Both McDougals were convicted in May of fraud in a case Starr brought.

James McDougal is cooperating with Starr, and his sentencing has been postponed twice. But Susan McDougal has accused Starr of political motivation in pursuing the investigation and has said she will not cooperate, because she fears he will charge her with perjury if she fails to incriminate the Clintons.
In asking a judge to reverse her contempt citation, Susan McDougal argued that cooperating with Starr would violate her constitutional rights.
